name: AIT Alert Data Set
provenance: Alerts produced by Suricata, Wazuh and AMiner over the AIT-LDSv2 testbeds; published on Zenodo (record 8263181). Generation code: github.com/ait-aecid/alert-data-set.
citation: AIT Alert Data Set, Zenodo record 8263181, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8263181, published 2023-08-18.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.notes: Attribution only; verified on the official Zenodo record page (2026-10-19). No NonCommercial/ShareAlike constraint on the alerts (unlike the AIT-LDSv2 raw logs).

access_conditions: Public download from Zenodo; no account required.
redistribution_conditions: Keep raw data under the git-ignored data/external/ (never committed). Redistribution permitted with attribution.
ground_truth: Attack time-windows per testbed (labels.csv: scenario,attack,start,end). This yields a reconstructed TIME_LABEL (an alert is 'attack' iff its timestamp falls in an attack phase), NOT a per-event causal label. The official per-event event_label is produced only by the AIT-ADS pipeline against AIT-LDSv2/AIT-NDS and is not included in this Zenodo record.
known_limitations: Synthetic lab testbeds, not production SOC traffic.
Alert volume and class balance depend on the detectors' configuration.
Ground truth is a TIME_LABEL (temporal co-occurrence), not causal: every alert during an attack window is labeled 'attack', including unrelated background noise.
event_label (per-event causal label) is NOT distributed in this record (only ait_ads.zip + labels.csv); obtaining it requires the AIT-ADS pipeline with AIT-LDSv2 + AIT-NDS.

Measured on fox/Wazuh (462,523 alerts; descriptive dataset statistics, NOT detection performance; diagnostic commit 931f3a0): 89.13% labeled attack, dominated by the 'dirb' web scan (98.51% of the attack class).

Near-trivial separability / leakage risk: a single generic rule (id 31101, 'Web server 400 error code') covers ~92% of attack alerts, and 8 rules cover 99.6% -> alert-level 'attack' is almost fully determined by rule identity.
High-value attack stages are rare on fox (privilege_escalation=10, dnsteal=381, cracking=554 alerts): the positive class is dominated by volumetric web-scan noise, not SOC-relevant intrusions.
~1.6k attack-labeled alerts fall on background rules (Dovecot auth success, IDS events, TLS) purely by time co-occurrence: clear temporal mislabels concentrated in auth/IDS signals.
